newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up slightly against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up slightly against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly at 8.2998 against the U.S. dollar on Monday with the announcement of the December interest rate subsidy having little impact on the market, dealers said.
The currency closed last Friday at 8.3001 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market.
The December interest rate subsidy was set by the central bank at 3.72 percent.
Dealers said the yuan was capped at the key 8.30 level by central bank intervention and was consolidating around 8.30 with a wait-and-see sentiment dominating the market.
The yuan opened little changed at 8.3002 and moved steadily below 8.3000 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day low of 8.3012 before rising to its highest level of 8.2987 late in the session.
Trading was dull with most done at about 8.3000, traders said.
"The yuan climbed above 8.30 at the close, but that has no significance for its direction in the short term," one dealer said. "The yuan is stable around 8.3000."
"The central bank announcement of an interest rate subsidy of 3.72 percent for December had little impacts on the yuan's movement," a second dealer said.
Dealers expect the yuan to stay around 8.3000 in the short term.
The yuan closed down at 7.4600 from 7.4300 against 100 Japanese yen and up slightly at 1.0735 from 1.0739 against the Hong Kong dollar.
